claim: Restructuring can be written as an operator set: relax a constraint, decompose a tight chunk, re-encode the problem, triggered after an impasse. Harder items are those that need a tighter constraint or chunk loosened.
agent_test: On items with a planted tight constraint, add an explicit relax/decompose/re-encode step after a detected impasse; compare solve rate to extra plain samples at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Whether restructuring is sudden depends on the measure and the statistic. Individual eye-tracking traces on matchstick problems: 27% sudden, 54% incremental, 19% unclear (Problem B solvers, 26 in first five minutes). Group ANOVA hides abrupt shifts; GAM and change-point models find them, but the sudden figure in Graf 2023 is simulated and the original data indicate a gradual shift. Gap search: in LLM traces, population accuracy is a ramp (d01), but answer-information arrives in sparse bursts at plan or reflection tokens (d02, d03); no change-point vs linear test on single traces exists.
agent_test: Log which problem parts each reasoning step names; fit change-point vs linear models to the trace and see which pattern predicts a later correct answer.

claim: Solvers who later succeed shift attention to the critical element late in the solving period (final third, around the 90% bin); non-solvers stay on the obvious parts.
agent_test: Detect a stuck frame by counting how often the same problem elements are re-named; trigger the operator when focus has not changed for N steps.

claim: Gradual hidden build-up exists before many insight solutions (word-pair relatedness, 250 ms anagram solvability, importance ratings), so flat progress ratings do not prove no progress. Not every study agrees (Smith and Kounios 1996 did not replicate gradual accumulation). Gap search: in LLMs a partial-trace answer distribution and a hidden-state probe predict later correctness (d01, d04), the same kind of gradual latent signal.
schema_part: G (progress monitor must not read flat as no progress)
agent_test: Compare a cheap solvability probe on partial states against final correctness; keep it only if it predicts success above chance.

claim: Warmth ratings jump just before insight answers: 76% of correct solutions came after a sudden jump, but 52% of incorrect ones did too (Metcalfe, second-hand). Gap search: primary paper opened (d22): Exp 1 had 19 usable of 26 subjects, correlations .26 and .23; Exp 2 had 73 students, 39 usable for warmth. Self-report insight on magic tricks showed no warmth difference (d23, N=51), so the pattern depends on how insight is defined.
agent_test: Ask the agent for a closeness score each step; test whether a jump predicts correctness better than chance.

claim: A sudden, certain, pleasant flip is not proof of a correct answer: 37% (417 of 1124) of wrong magic-trick solutions had Aha above the correct-solution mean; later work shows Aha judgments follow cues such as a correct first move.
schema_part: G (verify before commit; confidence is no stop signal)
agent_test: Add a verification gate after any confident sudden answer; measure wrong-but-confident rate with and without the gate at equal tokens.

claim: On average, self-labelled insight solutions are more accurate than analytic ones (d 0.4 to 1.85) and insight errors are mostly omissions while analytic errors are guesses. Aha and accuracy correlate r about 0.4 to 0.5 for insight problems and CRAs, near 0 for non-insight.
schema_part: G (complete answers deserve more trust than forced guesses)
agent_test: Compare accuracy of answers given at budget end after partial search against answers the agent flags as complete.

claim: Relaxing a constraint is necessary but not sufficient. Ten-penny: control 3/30, line hint 2/29, intersection hint 6/28, maximization hint 21/29 (72%). A search criterion plus progress test is needed; key hints on nine-dot do not reliably help.
schema_part: O (pair restructure with search criterion) + G (progress test)
agent_test: Run restructure-only vs restructure-plus-objective prompts on multi-step puzzles at equal tokens.

claim: What a hint or depiction changes matters more than added activity: handling pencils gave 27.3% vs 32.6% (ns); a picture showing operators can be decomposed lifted matchstick arithmetic from 46.7% to 79.3%; a hint after 5 min added only 11 points.
agent_test: Add a re-describe-in-another-form step (table, picture-like layout, opposite reading) and compare with a same-length neutral extra step.

claim: Concurrent verbalisation hurts a reinterpretation problem (deer problem 57% silent vs 13% verbalising) and helps a procedural one (30% vs 80%). Replication is mixed: Gilhooly and Fleck and Weisberg found no overshadowing. Gap search: verbal insight items showed no overshadowing (d18: .42 vs .40 solved, N=27 vs 26); Bayes reanalysis says some nulls are inconclusive (d19, abstract only); in LLMs CoT hurt 3 of 6 verbal-overshadowing tasks but none was an insight task (d17).
schema_part: G (do not force verbose step-by-step on reframing items)
agent_test: Compare forced long chain-of-thought vs short answer-first prompts on reframing vs procedural items at equal tokens.

claim: Sleep or rest alone did not help: no incubation or sleep effect on insight problems or magic tricks (N=77, F=0.008 and 0.047). A meta-analysis (not opened) reports a small positive incubation effect, larger with low-demand break tasks.
schema_part: none (no pause operator; spend effort on operators)
agent_test: Test a fresh second pass vs a pause with the same tokens elsewhere; only the first is meaningful for an LLM.

claim: Insight is a property of the solver state, not of the problem type: insight ratings vary within a type, Aha-accuracy links differ by task, and verbal and spatial insight problems resemble ordinary problems on dual-task and individual-difference tests.
schema_part: S (key on impasse signals, not category)
agent_test: Route by observed impasse (repeat, stall) not by task label; check the label-based router is no better.

claim: Special-process vs nothing-special is unresolved. Search with maximization and progress monitoring explain nine-dot and ten-penny; RCT replies that search heuristics cannot create a new space; networks produce abrupt switches without a special module. Authors favour a mix.
schema_part: O (restructure as one operator among search moves)
agent_test: Ablate the restructure operator while keeping progress-triggered search; if solve rate holds, the operator is not special.

claim: Abrupt, delayed, insight-like switches appear in plain gradient-trained networks (46/99 networks vs 49/99 humans; none at zero update noise) and in an active-inference model with a built-in model-reduction step. Suddenness can come from gradual silent learning.
schema_part: S (probe the gate: a check may open a switch)
agent_test: Insert a brief probe of a latent hypothesis before the full restructure and test whether it tips outcomes.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace 'wait/reconsider' shifts in LLMs are rare (6.31% pooled; 1.79% for a strict Aha) and go with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%, N=723,200). R1-Zero self-reflection is not positively correlated with accuracy; VLM aha moments occur in 8.3% of responses without reliable gain.
agent_test: Measure accuracy conditional on a wait token in our own traces, paired by item.

claim: The R1-Zero 'aha moment' is already present in base models (DeepSeek-V3-Base writes 'Aha'/'wait' before RL). Two other open replicas said to agree were not opened.
agent_test: Check the base-model rate of reflection phrases in our model before crediting scaffold effects.

claim: A forced second pass with a reconsideration cue improved MATH-500 from 32.2% to 40.6% (+8.41pp; 50,574 wrong-to-right vs 23,500 right-to-wrong), but compute is doubled and models are small; crosswords +0.45pp, Rush Hour near zero. Gap search: the +8.41pp doubles compute; compute-matched comparisons for other methods disagree (see K31).
agent_test: Compare one reconsideration pass against a second independent sample plus vote at equal tokens, gated on trace entropy or disagreement.

claim: Models often write the correct answer in their thought log and then do not commit (verification failure: 5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers across four models, literal string match). Gap search: the rate (5% to 39%) still rests on Mizumoto, but the phenomenon is supported by probes, injection and abandoned-thought counts (see K30).
schema_part: G (endorse-or-reject step; scan trace for earlier candidates)
agent_test: Scan our traces for gold answers appearing before the final answer; add a candidate-review step and measure recovery.

claim: Machine false insight exists: a confident flawed shortcut caused 77% to 100% of errors on adversarially evolved math problems; Mizumoto describe confident commitment to a wrong reframing qualitatively. Gap search: no rate of false insight with a verifier was found; decorative checks (d07) and sticky confident errors in people (d23) point to the risk.
agent_test: Add a constraint check after any shortcut and count caught errors at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs fixate on the default or decoy reading: Only Connect GPT-4 10-shot solved 6 original walls vs 59 randomised vs 471 with red herrings removed (of 494); BRAINTEASER best model 53% and 63% vs human 92%; creative questions lose 6 to 17 points against factual ones on the same knowledge.
agent_test: On decoy-laden items, force k distinct framings before answering; compare with k samples at equal tokens.

claim: More reasoning effort or a reasoning model helps on insight-type riddles but does not close the gap: NazoNazo non-reasoning 7.6% vs reasoning 17.6% vs human mean 52.9% (120-item subset); rebus puzzles GPT-5 60% vs gpt-4o 19%; CresOWLve GPT-5.4 nearly doubles from no thinking to medium effort.
agent_test: Run our insight set at several token budgets and plot the curve; check where a scaffold beats raw budget.

claim: Riddle and lateral benchmarks are contaminated or memorised: ChatGPT fails 45% of originals whose reconstructed twin it solves, quiz sources overlap training data, riddle items are public. Gap search: in SemEval-2024 Task 9, over 80% of leaderboard entries dropped when puzzles were reworded, even with 80% training data.
schema_part: G (use unseen, reworded twin items for any claim)
agent_test: Build a private reworded twin for each test item; report both scores.

claim: Unstructured two-agent chat explored more but discovered less on situation puzzles (N=82; 47% protocol failure, 53% coordination cost). Abstract only, preprint.
agent_test: Compare one scaffolded agent against two free-talking agents at equal tokens on situation puzzles.

claim: Self-verification in RL-trained VLMs underperforms simple majority voting (best-of-N with self-verification falls up to 16.7% for VLAA models). The same paper appears twice in the evidence files.
schema_part: G (prefer sampling plus vote or external check)
agent_test: Compare self-verify vs vote at equal tokens on our items.

claim: Pupil dilation rises before reported insight (about 200 ms before the report, also for wrong insights) and stays high in solvers during an incubation task. Primary papers not fully read.
agent_test: No agent test; design hint only.

claim: Chain-of-thought can lock in a long procedure and reduce use of shortcuts (n=6 per cell, no statistics); evidence is very weak.
schema_part: O (ask 'is there a shortcut?' before step-by-step)
agent_test: Test a shortcut-check pre-step on Einstellung-style math items with n of at least 50.

claim: Much of R1 'reflection' on AIME is shallow verification loops, and reflection helps only inside deductive inference; failed traces over- or under-use branching. One model, one contest.
schema_part: G (budget retries on re-framing, not re-checking)
agent_test: Count branch-and-backtrack vs re-check steps in our traces and relate each to success.

claim: No paper was found running Duncker's candle, nine-dot or matchstick problems on 2024-2026 LLMs with human norms; classic-paradigm LLM results are unmeasured (search budget was limited). Gap search: still no nine-dot or candle run on LLMs with human norms; closest are MacGyver (everyday fixedness, 2023 models, d20) and a children replication of the Duncker pre-use effect (d24) that gives a design to copy.
agent_test: Run nine-dot, candle and matchstick with matched human norms as our own held-out set.

claim: Explicit training of deduction, induction and abduction as separate meta-abilities beats waiting for emergent aha (over 10% relative gain over baseline, authors' own benchmarks); it is a training method, not a scaffold.
schema_part: O (name the inference type needed at an impasse)
agent_test: Prompt for abduction at impasse vs generic retry at equal tokens.

claim: Models hold the right answer or idea and do not use it. Hidden-state probes predict correctness of intermediate answers (ROC-AUC over 0.9 on AIME for R1-Distill-Qwen-32B; d04); over 70% of wrong responses contain a correct thought that was abandoned (d08); a ground-truth solution put into the trace is often ignored (d05); in one resampling case the right check was voiced and lowered accuracy (d02). Qualitative support is strong; the rate for current frontier models and a string-match-free measure are still missing.
schema_part: G (commit rule after a check against the original problem); state: endorse-or-reject step
agent_test: Run a separate endorse-or-reject call on every candidate that appeared in the thought log; count the wrong answers where a rejected candidate was correct, using an answer-matching judge instead of string match.

claim: At equal compute, whether a second look beats independent samples is contested. Intrinsic self-correction and debate lost to self-consistency at equal responses on 2023 models (GSM8K: 6 responses 85.3 vs debate 83.2; d11). A 1.5B distilled model gained more from 8x16K voted samples (41.0 on AIME24) than from 128K of sequential thinking (27.4; d12). Refinement chains beat parallel voting in 43 of 45 matched-token configurations, but chains were capped at 4096 tokens and one headline cell is misprinted (d13). No study uses an explicit restructure operator.
agent_test: Run three arms per item at identical total tokens on a 2026 frontier model: independent samples + vote, same-chain extension, and restructure-then-solve; report accuracy per 1K tokens and keep native-length chains.

claim: Re-encoding the problem before sampling beats plain sampling at the same number of paths, on easy arithmetic and with older models: RM-PoT at N=16 paths gave 80.4 / 69.1 / 88.0 vs self-consistency 77.3 / 64.9 / 87.6 on GSM8K / AQuA / SVAMP (d14); question-reformulation plus sampling averaged 83.0 vs 79.5 for plain self-consistency on GPT-3.5-turbo (d15). This is rewording, not constraint relaxation, and token counts are not matched.
agent_test: Replace some of N samples with samples from reworded or reordered versions of the problem and compare with N plain samples on reframing items at equal tokens.

claim: Which trigger starts a restructure is untested head-to-head. Candidates have separate evidence: token entropy forks are sparse and mark path choices (d10); confidence-based filtering saves 43-79% tokens vs majority voting at matched accuracy (d09); high thought-switch counts go with wrong answers and a penalty on switching raised AIME2024 pass@1 from 38.3 to 44.1 for QwQ (d08); a fixed-round restart on 5 situation puzzles won 4 of 5 vs 2 of 5 (d16, pilot). Switching often is a sign of failure, so a stall trigger should require some depth on the current line.
agent_test: Compare four triggers (same-element stall, entropy spike, sample disagreement, cheap solvability probe) plus a no-trigger control on the same items and tokens.

claim: Inside LLM traces, answer-relevant information is concentrated at a few steps, while average progress looks like a ramp. Mutual-information peaks at tokens like 'Wait' and 'Therefore' (d03); sentence-level thought anchors, mostly plan and backtrack sentences, with one case where expected accuracy jumped at a single method switch (d02); average accuracy and commitment rise with trace depth, steepest late (d01); high-entropy forking tokens are a minority (d10). Whether single traces show a sudden jump or a ramp has not been tested with change-point models.
schema_part: S (stall detection); O (restructure at a plan-change)
agent_test: Fit change-point and linear models to per-step progress (answer-distribution probe) across traces of a reframing item set; report the share of traces better explained by a jump.

claim: A latent-progress probe predicts later success in LLMs when you have access to the model or can truncate its trace: hidden-state probes give ROC-AUC over 0.9 (d04), early exit at threshold 0.85 saves about 24% tokens at 88.2% accuracy (d04), and truncated-trace answer distributions track final accuracy (d01). It does not yet show that a flat probe reliably precedes a restructure that works.
agent_test: Log a probe (answer distribution after forced stop) at fixed token checkpoints and test whether flat probes predict failure better than trace length alone.

claim: Most self-checks inside reasoning traces change nothing: only 5.4% of 1,000 human-annotated reflection steps were corrective (d06), and over 30% of steps in Kimi-K2.6 and nearly 60% in Qwen3.6-35B on MATH are decorative by causal score (d07). A verbal constraint check protects against a confident wrong shortcut only if its result gates the answer.
schema_part: G (checks must gate output); O (targeted verify)
agent_test: Measure false-insight rate with and without a gating constraint check against the original problem; use perturbation of the check text as a control.

claim: Early wrong steps anchor what follows. Longer wrong prefixes lowered later accuracy on AIME 2024 for a 1.5B model (d12); a weaker model's wrong partial trace pulls a stronger model toward the same wrong answer, with 13-32% less anchoring when the stronger model continues freely (d01); GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7% of the time and changed right to wrong more than wrong to right (d11). Restarting from a consolidated state helped in a 5-puzzle pilot (d16).
schema_part: O (restart over patch); G (do not trust earlier steps)
agent_test: Inject a wrong prefix of varying length into the scaffold and compare patch-in-place, restart-with-summary and fresh sample on recovery at equal tokens.

claim: Metcalfe and Wiebe 1987 is a small effect: Exp 1 had 19 usable of 26 subjects with correlations .26 (t(18)=2.02) and .23 (t(18)=1.63, one-tailed); Exp 2 had 73 recruited, 48 usable for feeling-of-knowing and 39 for warmth (d22). With self-reported insight on 32 magic tricks (N=51), warmth did not differ although insight answers were more accurate and more confident (d23). Suddenness of feeling is therefore not a safe signal of progress or of correctness.
schema_part: S (do not rely on felt sudden progress)
agent_test: Treat a confident late jump in the agent's own stated certainty as a trigger to verify; test whether verified jumps are more often right than unverified jumps.

claim: The pre-use effect behind Duncker's candle problem replicates in a children's box task: 18% of 6-7-year-olds offered the box solution after pre-use vs 89% without; 5-year-olds were unaffected (64% vs 65%; 60 children, 10 per cell; d24). Duncker 1945, Adamson 1952 and Glucksberg 1962 original numbers were not obtained. LLM version is cheap: show the object's standard use earlier in context, then test.
agent_test: Pre-use manipulation on LLMs: first mention the object in its usual role, then pose the problem; compare solve rate with no pre-use and with a divergent-uses step.

claim: A divergent step before convergence raises the number of efficient solutions for GPT-4 on everyday fixedness problems (30.1% to 36.6% on 180 problems, and fewer infeasible ones), while self-reflection mostly removes infeasible ones (d20). Smaller models (Claude2, Llama2-13b) did not gain from self-reflection. 2023 models; reading of a figure.
agent_test: Divergent-then-convergent step vs plain retry at equal tokens on a held-out set of fixedness items with human norms.

claim: Benchmark ceilings on lateral puzzles come from fitting the benchmark, not from restructuring: with 80% of BRAINTEASER available for training, SemEval-2024 top systems reached 0.983 overall, yet over 80% of leaderboard entries lost accuracy on reworded semantic or context twins (drops up to 0.28 and 0.34) and only one word-puzzle model held up on all three variants (d21).
agent_test: Report group-based accuracy over original, semantic and context twins on a private set; drop public-train fine-tuned entries from the comparison.
